modelId.description: Target name for {@link MlModel.id} used for operation.

subjectId.description: Target name for {@link MlSubject.id} for which the output is computed.

statusLabel.description: Target name for {@link MlModel.Route.Status.label} of {@link MlModel.Route} used for operation.

statusTags.description: Target name for {@link MlModel.Route.Status.tags} of {@link MlModel.Route} used for operation.

outputTimestamp.description: Target name for timestamp of operation.

outputNames.description:
The {@link MlPipeline#outNames pipeline outputs} that are processed by this handler.
If `null` and if there are multiple outputs to the pipeline, an error is thrown.

columnMapping.description:
Mapping to rename the metadata columns {@link MlModel.OutputHandlerMetaColumns} and data columns of an
instance of {@link Data} in the output handlers. If an output column is mapped to `null` (or `None` in Python),
it is dropped.

As a convenience, if a user provides a mapping involving one of the special {@link MlModel.OutputHandlerMetaColumns},
then the user-provided mapping will take precedence.

Additionally, if a user provides a mapping for a column that does not exist in the output data, that column
mapping will be ignored.

For {@link MlModel.CSVOutputHandler}
- If an output column is not mapped, best-effort mapping is performed to match the CSV header, and any unmatched
columns will be dropped.

For {@link MlModel.DbOutputHandler}
- If an output column is not mapped, best-effort mapping is performed to match the {@link MlModel.DbOutputHandler#targetType}
declared fieldnames, and any unmatched columns will be dropped.

mergeField.description:
If provided, then any columns not mapped in {@link #columnMapping} will be merged into a single field in the
target type, with the provided field name.
The field type should be a map with string keys. It will be populated with a map, where the key represents
the column name from the handled output and the value represents the corresponding value in that column.
NOTE: if this field is set, then there will not be any automatic column mapping of unspecified columns!

sourceCollection.description: The {@link FileSourceCollection} in which the CSV files are placed.

filenamePrefix.description:
The prefix of the filename generated for each call to {@link process}.
The fields used to populate the template are derived from the `route` argument.

title:
An {@link MlModel.OutputHandler} that writes the output into a CSV file.

**Important note**: the type of the pipeline output values must be {@link Data}.

This handler generates a file in the {@link FileSourceCollection#inboxUrl inbox} of the {@link sourceCollection}.
The filename is the concatenation of the {@link filenamePrefix} and the current timestamp, for example:
`<sourceCollectionInbox>/project1--model1--1658245954.csv`

The header of the CSV is the following:
```
modelId,statusLabel,statusTags,subjectId,outputTimestamp,field1,field2,...
```
where:
 - `modelId` is the ID of the {@link MlModel};
 - `statusLabel` is the {@link MlModel.Route.Status.Label status label} of the route;
 - `statusTags` is a string representing the (optional) {@link MlModel.Route.Status#tags} of the route;
 - `subjectId` is the ID of the {@link MlSubject} for which the output is computed;
 - `outputTimestamp` is the timestamp for which the output is computed (optional, it is present only when
    there is a {@link Feature#TIMESTAMP timestamp} column in the {@link Data} to process);
 - `field1,field2,...` correspond to the mapped columns of the output to process (see {@link columnMapping}).

Each row of the CSV correspond to a row in the {@link Data} object processed by the handler.

**NOTE**: This handler only supports single pipeline output, so `outputNames` should be singleton or empty.

Usage:
```python
handler = c3.MlModel.CsvOutputHandler(
    outputNames=["predictions"],
    columnMapping={
        "mean": "value"
    },
    sourceCollection="Prediction_Collection"
)
```
name: MlModel.CsvOutputHandler
